title: Top Dodgers prospect River Ryan suffers hamstring injury, delaying MLB return: Sources
content:
SAN DIEGO — The wait for River Ryan’s return to the big leagues continues. The Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander, one of the highest-regarded pitching prospects in the sport, is going to be placed on the minor-league injured list with a hamstring issue, according to league sources who were not authorized to speak publicly about the situation.

It’s unclear how serious the issue is for Ryan, who ranked as the No. 19 prospect in baseball in The Athletic’s midseason rankings. He did not make his scheduled start with Triple-A Oklahoma City this week and has returned to Arizona to rehab his second hamstring injury already in 2026.

Ryan has a 4.46 ERA in eight starts this season while flashing premium stuff, including a fastball that touches triple digits and a six-pitch arsenal that got him 43 strikeouts in 36 1/3 innings. This has been his first game action since 2024, when Ryan made his brief big-league debut and tore his ulnar collateral ligament in his fourth major-league start.

Ryan’s immense promise has made him the subject of fan fervor, with some clamoring for him to join a rotation that ranks second in baseball with a 3.25 ERA. Dodgers officials have pushed back on Ryan’s timeline, saying they need the 28-year-old converted infielder to build up a foundation to withstand a starter’s workload. While there hasn’t been a hard cap set on Ryan’s innings, the Dodgers surely want to make sure they don’t tax Ryan too much in his first season back from Tommy John surgery as well.

“Especially with our young pitchers, as much patience as we can exercise when they’re coming back from a major surgery, the better,” president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said to The Athletic last week. “The level of intensity is different at the major league level than it is in the minor leagues.”

Ryan’s setback at least temporarily removes him from the immediate starting picture.

The Dodgers also won’t have Blake Snell back before the All-Star break, manager Dave Roberts confirmed on Friday. Snell threw his first full bullpen session Friday at Dodger Stadium, throwing 15 fastballs for the first time since undergoing the “NanoNeedle” procedure to remove bone spurs from his left elbow.

Katie Woo contributed to this story.
